analysis: Hypothesis: trend and mean-reversion parameters capture complementary behavior, while an adaptive allocator may improve their balance across regimes. Treat budget 20 as candidate evaluations: 6 trend, 6 mean-reversion, 6 adaptive, and 2 baselines (equal-weight allocation and a fixed trend/mean-reversion mix). Evaluate every candidate on the same four frozen walk-forward validation folds within 2021–2024, fitting only on each fold’s preceding training data. No results are supplied; no ranking is established.
next_actions: Freeze candidate definitions, fold boundaries, baselines, cost assumptions, and ranking rules before evaluation. Rank by median net risk-adjusted performance across folds, breaking ties by lower worst-fold drawdown and then lower turnover. Report each fold’s returns, volatility, drawdown, turnover, and baseline differences; inspect parameter sensitivity and allocator stability. If costs are unavailable, label results gross and report explicit cost sensitivities. Do not retune using validation-fold outcomes.
risks: Twenty candidates and four folds provide limited evidence and may encourage selection overfitting. Regime dependence, turnover, transaction costs, unstable allocator weights, and leakage can distort comparisons. Universe, parameter ranges, fold boundaries, cost assumptions, and scoring rules remain unspecified. Development validation does not establish holdout performance or future profit.
